headline: Magnitude 7.0 Earthquake Kills at Least 16 in Tibet's Baqen County
summary: A magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck Baqen County in Nagqu, Tibet, at 22:33 local time on October 22, killing at least 16 people and injuring over 50. The quake collapsed more than 339 homes, prompting deployment of over 1,600 rescuers.

headline: Hurricane Vance Holds at Category 2 South of Puerto Vallarta, Landfall Possible Oct 26-27
summary: Hurricane Vance remained a Category 2 storm with about 110mph winds roughly 365 miles south-southwest of Acapulco as of Oct 24, moving slowly north-northwest. Forecasters say it could make landfall near Puerto Vallarta, Mexico on Oct 26-27, or it could remain offshore.

headline: Typhoon Rosal (Champi) Exits Philippine Area After Weakening, No Landfall
summary: Typhoon Rosal, known internationally as Champi — which earlier caused 527 injuries and mass power outages in Taiwan — exited the Philippine Area of Responsibility on the morning of Oct 24 after weakening to 120km/h winds from a peak of 215km/h. The storm did not make landfall in the Philippines but brought moderate to heavy rain to Batanes.

headline: Bay of Bengal Depression Forecast to Strengthen Into Cyclone, Threatening Andhra Pradesh Coast
summary: India's Meteorological Department said a low-pressure system in the Bay of Bengal intensified into a depression as of the night of Oct 24, centered near 15.5N, 91.0E. It is forecast to become a cyclonic storm by Oct 26 and reach the north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coast around Oct 28. Sri Lanka is not expected to be directly hit but may see increased rain and wind.

headline: Nigeria Confirms Bundibugyo Ebola Strain Matches DRC Outbreak, 44 Contacts Monitored
summary: Nigerian health officials confirmed on Oct 20 that the imported Ebola case matches the Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain from the DRC outbreak that began in May 2026, marking the first spread of that outbreak to West Africa. Forty-four contacts have been identified and are under monitoring.

headline: China Reports Two More Human H9N2 Avian Flu Cases in Children, Both Recovered
summary: China reported two additional human cases of H9N2 avian influenza in 1-year-old girls, one with poultry exposure in Henan and one linked to a live poultry market in Guangdong. Symptom onset was in late August and early September 2026, and both children recovered without hospitalization.

headline: Houthi Missile Strike on Yemen Training Camp Death Toll Revised Up to 73, Deadliest of War's New Phase
summary: The toll from the October 19 Houthi ballistic missile strike on the Martyr Ahmed al-Sulaimani Training Centre in Shabwa, Yemen was revised upward to 73 killed, with over 200 wounded and 14 missing. Victims were mostly recruits aged 18-20 for a new 'Rapid Intervention' force; it is the deadliest single strike since Yemen's civil war resumed roughly three months ago.

headline: Russia Strikes Kyiv With Three Waves of Ballistic Missiles Hours After Witkoff-Putin Meeting
summary: Russia fired 21 ballistic missiles plus drones at Kyiv overnight on October 21-22 in three waves, killing one person and injuring up to 24. The attack damaged an ambulance station, a monastery, and metro bridge infrastructure, coming hours after US envoy Steve Witkoff met Putin in St. Petersburg.

headline: France Deploys 70,000 Police, Shuts Louvre and Metro Stations Ahead of Nationwide Protests
summary: Ahead of Oct 24 nationwide protests, France deployed about 70,000 police and gendarmes, closed the Louvre, Musée d'Orsay, Picasso Museum and Grand Palais, shut over 24 Metro stations, and banned demonstrations in Lyon, Nice and Montpellier while allowing restricted marches in Paris and Marseille. The measures follow rioting and looting on Oct 17 that led to roughly 2,700 detentions.

headline: Hundreds of Thousands Join Coordinated Cost-of-Living Protests Across France, Italy, Spain, Portugal, Albania
summary: Simultaneous demonstrations swept Europe on Oct 24: France saw 410,000-800,000 protesters and about 1,000 arrests; Italy saw protests in Milan, Rome, Turin, Bologna and Florence with 371 briefly detained; Spain's Madrid saw pension protests; Portugal saw housing-crisis demonstrations; and Albania saw anti-government protests. Clashes with police involved tear gas and water cannons in several cities.

headline: Saudi Arabia Postpones Flagship FII Investment Conference to 2027 Citing Security Situation
summary: Saudi Arabia postponed its flagship Future Investment Initiative conference, originally scheduled for October 26-29, to 2027, citing the security situation following Houthi missile attacks including the Riyadh airport strike. The airport has remained closed; scheduled speakers included Jamie Dimon, Jane Fraser, David Solomon and Larry Fink.

headline: Brazil's Runoff Polls Close With Lula-Bolsonaro Race Still Too Close to Call
summary: Polls closed at 5pm Brasília time on Oct 25 in Brazil's presidential runoff between Lula da Silva and Flávio Bolsonaro. No winner has been confirmed in available reporting, with the race described as razor-thin. Results are expected to be announced later in the evening.

headline: 150,000 Rally in Belgrade in Final Push Before Serbia's Oct. 25 Election
summary: Around 150,000 people rallied in Belgrade on October 21-22, the final demonstration by the student-backed opposition before Sunday's election. Civil society groups warned the election environment falls short of free-and-fair standards.

headline: Putin Agrees to Resume Trilateral Ukraine Peace Talks, Releases Detained American
summary: Putin met US envoy Steve Witkoff in St. Petersburg on October 21, during which Russia released American Stephen Hubbard, detained since 2022. A US official said Russia and Ukraine agreed to resume trilateral technical peace talks after November 10.

headline: CENTCOM Marks 100 Days of Naval Blockade on Iran as IRGC Maintains Hormuz Closure
summary: US CENTCOM marked 100 days of its naval blockade of Iranian ports on October 22, saying it has blocked roughly $25 billion in Iranian crude exports. Iran's IRGC had earlier declared the Strait of Hormuz closed "until US conditions are met" and warned of strikes on US-escorted vessels.

headline: Islamic State-Linked Fighters Kill at Least 48 Civilians Near Menaka, Eastern Mali
summary: On October 18, fighters from the Islamic State Sahel Province (ISSP) raided Idaksahak pastoralist communities near Menaka, killing at least 48 civilians. The attack was reportedly carried out in retaliation for suspected informants aiding a Malian army drone strike.

headline: Armed Men Storm Libya's National Audit Bureau to Install Rival Deputy Head
summary: Masked armed men stormed the Tripoli headquarters of Libya's National Audit Bureau on Oct 21 to forcibly install Anwar al-Housh as deputy head under an appointment by the High Council of State. The Bureau suspended all operations in response. The move was condemned by UNSMIL, the United States and the United Kingdom.

headline: Senegal's 72-Hour General Strike Disrupts Healthcare, Schools, Transport Before Youth Olympics
summary: Senegal's Trade Union Front, representing 13 unions, led a 72-hour general strike from Oct 21-23 over wages, pensions and labor codes, disrupting hospitals, schools and Dakar's bus network, prompting a military deployment to maintain minimal transit service. The action came days before Dakar hosts the Youth Olympic Games opening Oct 31; the government called the strike unlawful.

headline: Argentine Judge Dismisses Fraud Probe Into Milei Over $LIBRA Meme-Coin Collapse
summary: Federal Judge Martinez De Giorgi dismissed the criminal fraud investigation into President Milei and his sister Karina over the February 2025 collapse of the $LIBRA memecoin, ruling the events did not constitute a criminal offense. A parallel probe into promoter Hayden Davis was also dismissed.

headline: 18-Floor Unfinished Building Collapses in Nairobi, Several Missing
summary: An 18-floor unfinished building with occupied ground-floor and basement shops collapsed on 9th Street in Nairobi's Eastleigh area on Oct 23. Seven people were reported missing or trapped, one woman was rescued alive, and 66 of 67 construction workers escaped. Kenya Red Cross, the military and county emergency teams are responding; the building had no occupation certificate.

headline: India Issues Red Alert for Kerala Districts as Heavy Rain Raises Flood and Landslide Risk
summary: India's Meteorological Department issued red alerts for Malappuram, Kozhikode and Wayanad districts on Oct 25, and for Idukki and Palakkad on Oct 26, warning of rainfall exceeding 204.4mm in 24 hours with flash flood and landslide risk. Schools were closed in the Oct 25 red-alert districts.

headline: Philippine Peso Hits 31st Record Low of 2026 at P63.615 per Dollar
summary: The Philippine peso closed at a fresh record low of 63.615 to the US dollar on Oct 23, its 31st record low this year. The decline was driven by elevated oil prices, September inflation of 7.2%, and broader dollar strength amid geopolitical tension.

headline: Shooting Outside Memphis Event Center Wounds Five to Six, Suspect Arrested
summary: A fight outside an event center in the Oakhaven area of Memphis, Tennessee escalated into a shooting around 2am on Oct 24-25, wounding five to six people. Suspect Kendell Catron, 24, was arrested and charged with four counts of aggravated assault.
